ownership.title: Three responsibilities
ownership.explanation: The tab holds a read model for synchronous rendering. The SharedWorker owns acquisition and mutation. Pure read definitions run in both places; credentials and HTTP stay in the owner integration.

nodes.title: Component
nodes.summary: Describe what the view needs. Render it with public hooks.

nodes.title: Domain
nodes.summary: Define how backend responses, permissions, and operations work.

nodes.title: Browser host
nodes.summary: Connect tabs to one owner, with events and optional storage.

acquisition.title: From need to knowledge
acquisition.explanation: The shared owner combines demand from tabs and imperative readers, subtracts known information, and reuses in-flight work. It compares declared backend capabilities and costs. Responses establish facts; missing information may require another source.

nodes.title: Combine demand
nodes.summary: Collect what active consumers across tabs still need.

nodes.title: Reuse knowledge
nodes.summary: Subtract known facts and account for work already in flight.

nodes.title: Compare sources
nodes.summary: Choose compatible reads using coverage, permissions, and cost.

nodes.title: Observe and reconsider
nodes.summary: Publish actual evidence, then plan for any remaining gaps.

proposals.title: A proposal sits above confirmed facts
proposals.explanation: Removing a proposal does not restore a saved old snapshot. Success must be supported by backend evidence; a partial or unknown outcome cannot be rewritten as complete success.

nodes.title: Confirmed: open
nodes.summary: The service last confirmed this task is open.

nodes.title: Proposed: done
nodes.summary: The component previews completion while the action runs.

nodes.title: New evidence arrives
nodes.summary: Events can change the confirmed task beneath the preview.

nodes.title: Reveal the latest facts
nodes.summary: When the preview ends, show current facts, not an old snapshot.

baseline.title: An editor keeps its concurrency baseline
baseline.explanation: Reload explicitly discards the draft and prepares a new baseline. Known read revocation removes protected values; write-only loss keeps readable values and disables saving.

nodes.title: Prepare + ETag
nodes.summary: Read the saved notes and their version together.

nodes.title: Keep a draft
nodes.summary: Keep typed changes with that original version.

nodes.title: External change
nodes.summary: A teammate’s update changes shared facts, not dirty input.

nodes.title: Save conditionally
nodes.summary: Send draft + original version. A conflict preserves the draft.

recovery.title: Recovery investigates what happened
recovery.explanation: A missing response, missing journal, or missing operation history does not prove that the operation never happened. Recovery is not an instruction to submit again. A lock protects owner exclusivity; a heartbeat timeout cannot transfer ownership.

nodes.title: Checkpoint
nodes.summary: Record possible submission before sending, when storage works.

nodes.title: Submit once
nodes.summary: A lost response does not tell us whether the work happened.

nodes.title: Restore context
nodes.summary: Restore the action record after access is established.

nodes.title: Investigate
nodes.summary: Check what happened. Do not send the command again.
